RFC5838-2.3-1.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29. New negative TestRFC5838NonConformingPrefixNotInRouteComputation drives v6BuildRoutes on an IPv4-unicast AF with one Intra-Area-Prefix-LSA holding a /24 and a 64-bit prefix: exactly one route, the /24, so the conforming sibling proves the LSA was read (revert record on v6PrefixToNetip). Positive TestIPv4OverV3BuildRoutes has no record but is exact. Missing: the other route-computation inputs. The inter-area-prefix path and the AS-external/NSSA record path in afstrategy_v6.go each call v6PrefixToNetip with their own ok check; dropping either check stays green, since no tagged unit feeds a non-conforming inter-area or external prefix.

RFC5838-2.4-1.note: Forbidden behaviour (a): a non-default-AF instance accepting a Hello with the AF-bit clear. (b) TestAFBitGatesFullNonDefault dispatches that Hello on an IPv4-unicast instance and asserts neighborSnapshot() is empty (a processed Hello would create an Init neighbor), then the same Hello with SetAF() yields one neighbor, isolating the AF-bit as the only difference.

RFC5838-2.4-2.note: Forbidden behaviour (a): the base IPv6-unicast AF discarding a Hello whose AF-bit is clear. (b) TestAFBitIgnoredDefaultAF dispatches an AF-bit-less Hello to the default IPv6-unicast engine and asserts neighborSnapshot() has one row, so an applied AF-bit check goes red. Single-polarity marker holds (the base AF has no reject path).

RFC5838-2.6-1.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29. NSSA-LSA origination is proven both ways: TestRFC5838IPv4AFNSSAForwardingAddressIsIPv4 decodes the originated NSSA-LSA for IPv4 unicast and IPv4 multicast AFs and reads 192.0.2.7 in the leading 32 bits; TestRFC5838IPv4AFNSSANeverEncodesIPv6ForwardingAddress offers only an IPv6 address and reads no FA; revert records on forwardingAddressForAF. Missing: the AS-external-LSA clause. Ze's redistributed Type-5 (v6OriginateExternalLSA) carries no FA, but the translated Type-5 does: translateNSSAV6 (nssa.go) copies a RECEIVED Type-7's 16-byte FA through v6UsableForwardingAddress, an IPv6-only check, with no address-family test, into v6OriginateTranslatedExternal. On an IPv4 AF a peer's Type-7 with an IPv6 FA would be re-originated in Ze's own AS-external-LSA. No test covers that path; the handoff's claim that the translated FA is always set by forwardingAddressForAF holds only for Ze's own Type-7s. Probable defect, reported.

RFC5838-2.6-2.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29. The positive reads all 16 bytes of the originated NSSA-LSA FA (IPv4 then 96 zero bits) for both IPv4 AFs, with a revert record on forwardingAddressForAF. The {single-polarity} annotation argues no non-zero-trailing path exists; that holds for forwardingAddressForAF but not for the translated AS-external-LSA: translateNSSAV6 copies a received Type-7's FA verbatim with no AF check, so a peer's FA with non-zero trailing bits reaches Ze's own Type-5 on an IPv4 AF. The annotation's argument is therefore incomplete and the translation path is untested.

RFC5838-2.8-1.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29. Positive TestV6VirtualEndpointResolvesGlobalAddress resolves global /128 LA addresses on both ends. Negatives cover both ends: the existing neighbor-side link-local-only case and new TestRFC5838VirtualLinkRequiresLocalGlobalAddress (this router advertises only fe80::1, neighbor global) which fails to resolve. v6ResolveVirtualEndpointLocked requires sok && dok and v6RouterGlobalAddr refuses non-global addresses; revert record on the resolver.
